exercises.prompt: At hotel reception, say: “I have a reservation under the name Marta Silva.”
exercises.explanation: Use the fixed hotel phrase «Tenho uma reserva em nome de…». You can also add «Eu», but Portuguese often leaves the subject out.
acceptedAnswers: Eu tenho uma reserva em nome de Marta Silva.

exercises.prompt: At a hotel, ask politely for a room for two nights.
exercises.explanation: «Queria…» is a very common polite chunk in Portugal for requests. Learn it as a whole phrase.
acceptedAnswers: Eu queria um quarto para duas noites.
Queria um quarto para duas noites, por favor.

exercises.prompt: At reception, ask if breakfast is included.
exercises.explanation: For hotel services, this fixed question is very common: «O pequeno-almoço está incluído?». Use «está», not «é».

exercises.prompt: Call reception and report this room problem: the air conditioning does not work.
exercises.explanation: This is a useful whole sentence for a problem in the room. The negative goes before the verb: «não funciona».

exercises.prompt: Your room has a problem. Ask hotel staff politely to move you to another room.
exercises.explanation: Use the fixed request «Pode trocar-me de quarto?». Learn it as a chunk for hotel situations.
acceptedAnswers: Pode mudar-me de quarto?
Pode-me trocar de quarto?

exercises.prompt: Ask a receptionist politely to recommend a nearby restaurant.
exercises.explanation: This polite question is very useful when travelling. «Aqui perto» means “near here”.
acceptedAnswers: Pode recomendar-me um restaurante aqui perto?

exercises.prompt: The receptionist answers: «É no segundo andar.» Ask where the lift is.
exercises.explanation: To ask for a location, use «Onde fica…?». This is the natural phrase for places inside a building.
acceptedAnswers: Onde é que fica o elevador?
Onde é o elevador?
Onde é que é o elevador?

exercises.prompt: The receptionist answers: «É às onze.» Ask at what time check-out is.
exercises.explanation: For times, use «A que horas…?». Here you are asking about the hotel’s departure time.
acceptedAnswers: A que horas tenho de fazer o check-out?
A que horas é que é o check-out?

exercises.prompt: At the station, the clerk answers: «Na linha três.» Ask which line the train to Coimbra is on.
exercises.explanation: Use «Em que linha…?» to ask about the line or platform. This is a fixed travel question worth learning as a whole.
acceptedAnswers: Em que linha parte o comboio para Coimbra?

exercises.prompt: At the airport, the staff member answers: «Na porta quinze.» Ask where the boarding gate is.
exercises.explanation: At the airport, «porta de embarque» is the boarding gate. You can ask with «Onde é…?» or «Onde fica…?».
acceptedAnswers: Onde fica a porta de embarque?

exercises.prompt: You are speaking to reception. Fill the two gaps.
exercises.explanation: Use the polite request chunk «Pode…?» with staff. In «trocar-me de quarto», the preposition is «de».
exercises.template: O ar condicionado não funciona. ___ trocar-me ___ quarto?

exercises.prompt: A local is giving you directions. Fill the two gaps.
exercises.explanation: These are contractions: «a + a = à» in «à esquerda» and «a + o = ao» in «ao lado».
exercises.template: Siga sempre em frente e vire ___ esquerda. O museu fica ___ lado de um banco.

exercises.prompt: At the station, fill the two gaps to ask about the train.
exercises.explanation: Use «A que horas…?» for time and «em que linha» for the line or platform. These are common travel chunks.
exercises.template: ___ horas parte o próximo comboio? E ___ que linha é?

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: At the airport, «atrasado» means “delayed”. It is the usual word for a late flight.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: In this phrase, the natural word is «fotografia». Learn «Pode tirar-nos uma fotografia?» as a useful whole chunk.
exercises.sentence: Can you take a **photo** of us?

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: «Noite» is feminine, so “two” must be «duas»: «um quarto para duas noites». «Dois» goes with masculine nouns.

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: The natural fixed phrase is «aqui perto» for “near here”. «Próximo» is not the right word in this chunk.

exercises.prompt: Answer about yourself.
exercises.explanation: To say how you travel somewhere, use «Vou de…». This is a simple way to talk about your transport.
exercises.question: Como vais para o aeroporto?

exercises.prompt: At hotel reception. Put the lines in order.
exercises.explanation: At check-in, you normally give your reservation name first, then ask practical questions. Learn these service phrases as whole chunks.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Boa tarde. Tenho uma reserva em nome de Ana Costa.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Um momento, por favor. Sim, para duas noites.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sim, está incluído. O check-out é até às onze.

exercises.prompt: Ask a passer-by politely to take a photo of you and your friend.
exercises.explanation: Use «tirar uma fotografia» for taking a photo. «-nos» means “us”, so this is the natural phrase for two people.
acceptedAnswers: Pode tirar-nos uma foto?
Pode-nos tirar uma fotografia?

exercises.prompt: At hotel reception, say formally that your room is not clean.
exercises.explanation: Use «não está limpo» to report a problem right now. Learn the whole sentence as a useful hotel complaint.

exercises.prompt: You are at a hotel. Ask staff formally to send someone to your room.
exercises.explanation: With hotel staff, «Pode...?» is a polite request. Learn «mandar alguém ao quarto» as one chunk.

exercises.prompt: You need extra towels at the hotel. Fill the two gaps.
exercises.explanation: After «precisar», Portuguese uses «de»: «preciso de». «Toalhas» is plural because you want more than one.

exercises.prompt: At reception, ask formally if they can wake you up at seven o’clock.
exercises.explanation: Learn «Pode acordar-me…?» as a polite request chunk: «-me» (me) goes after the verb. «Às sete» = at seven (a + as).
acceptedAnswers: Pode-me acordar às sete?

exercises.prompt: At the airport, ask staff formally where the check-in desk is.
exercises.explanation: Ask for a place with «Onde é...?» or «Onde fica...?»; «balcão de check-in» is the fixed airport term.
exercises.givenAnswer: É ali, ao fundo do hall.
acceptedAnswers: Onde fica o balcão de check-in?

exercises.prompt: You have landed. Ask formally where you can collect your luggage.
exercises.explanation: «Posso» makes the question practical and polite. «Levantar a bagagem» is a common airport chunk in Portugal.
acceptedAnswers: Onde é que posso levantar a minha bagagem?

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: «Mala» is feminine, so the adjective is «pesada». Choose the form that agrees with the noun.

exercises.prompt: At airport security, ask formally if you can take this in hand luggage.
exercises.explanation: Use «bagagem de mão» for hand luggage. Learn the whole question as a fixed airport phrase.

exercises.prompt: You point to a place on the map. Ask a local if it is possible to go there on foot.
exercises.explanation: «Dá para...?» is a very common travel phrase meaning “is it possible to...?”. It is best learned as a chunk.
exercises.givenAnswer: Sim, claro. Demora uns dez minutos.

exercises.prompt: On the metro, ask staff formally whether you need to change lines.
exercises.explanation: «Fazer transbordo» means to change buses, trains or metro lines. Learn the whole question as a transport chunk.
acceptedAnswers: Tenho que fazer transbordo?
É preciso fazer transbordo?

exercises.prompt: Before getting on, ask formally if this bus goes to the airport.
exercises.explanation: With transport, use «vai para» to ask the destination. «Autocarro» is the European Portuguese word.
acceptedAnswers: Este autocarro vai ao aeroporto?

exercises.prompt: At the station, check formally if this is the right platform.
exercises.explanation: At Portuguese train stations the platform is called «linha» (feminine), so you say «a linha certa». Learn the question as a chunk.
acceptedAnswers: Esta é a linha certa?

exercises.prompt: At the ticket office, ask staff formally which ticket they recommend.
exercises.explanation: This short question is polite and useful when there are several ticket options. Learn it as a whole chunk.
acceptedAnswers: Que bilhete me recomenda?

exercises.prompt: At the station, say formally that you would like a return ticket to Faro.
exercises.explanation: «Ida e volta» means a return ticket. «Queria...» is a polite way to ask for something in stations and shops.
acceptedAnswers: Queria um bilhete de ida e volta para Faro, por favor.

exercises.prompt: A local is giving you directions to the museum. Fill the three gaps.
exercises.explanation: «Vire à direita» is the polite instruction “turn right” (learn it as a chunk) and «em frente de» means “opposite”.
exercises.template: Para o museu, ___ à direita. Fica ___ frente ___ uma farmácia.

exercises.prompt: You are lost in town. Ask a local to show you on the map and whether it is far. Fill the two gaps.
exercises.explanation: «Pode mostrar-me…?» is a polite request chunk (the «-me» means “me”), and «É longe daqui?» asks if it is far from here.
exercises.template: Desculpe, não conheço a cidade. Pode ___ no mapa? É ___ daqui?

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: «Estação» is feminine, so the article here is «a». The natural phrase is «Onde fica a estação de comboios?».

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: «Mala» is feminine, so «pesada» must also be feminine. «Pesado» would go with a masculine noun.

exercises.prompt: At hotel reception when leaving. Put the dialogue in order.
exercises.explanation: «Quero fazer o check-out» starts the exchange. The receptionist then asks for the key and finishes the stay.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bom dia. Quero fazer o check-out.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Claro. Tem a chave do quarto?

exercises.explanation: These are useful whole phrases for travel problems, directions and goodbyes. Match the Portuguese chunks to their English meanings.
